Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II Bldg., cor EDSA Mapagmahal Street, Diliman, Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 22 S. 2010 March 10, 2010 MARILYN L. DELA CRUZ MLGOO, Municipality of Labrador Province of Pangasinan Dear Ms. DeLa Cruz: This pertains to your letter seeking the Department's legal opinion, on the following issues, which we hereunder quote: "(1) Is there a need to declare the position of Mr. Escano vacant so that the Barangay Council can recommend and the Municipal Mayor appoint his replacement? If so, who will declare it vacant and how? (2) Can not the Barangay Council recommend and the Municipal Mayor appoint the replacement of Mr. Escano outright sans the declaration of vacany in the said position considering that he has not been reporting for work anymore since May 2008?" Per your letter, it appears that on May 17, 2008, Mr. Teofisto P. Escano, a Sangguniang Barangay Member of Ugong, Labrador, Pangasinan, suffered a stroke resulting from his non- attendance to sessions and non-performance from his duties and responsibilities. On November 9, 2008, the Barangay Council of Ugong passed Resolutions No. 028-2008, requesting the Municipal Health Officer thru Mayor Ernesto L. Acain to conduct a medical examination on Mr. Escano to determine his physical status to go back to work. On February 5, 2009, Mayor Acain also wrote Mr. Escano to submit himself for Medical Check-up before the Municipal Health Office or to any other authorized physicians. Up to the date of your letter, no information was sent by Mr. Escano to the Sangguniang Barangay or to Mayor Acain as to his physical status to go back to work. Hence, your queries. We shall answer your queries in one (1) discussion since they are related. In reply thereto, allow us first to restate the pertinent provision of the Local Government Code. Section 44 provides and we quote: "Sec. 44. Permanent vacancies in the offices of the Governor, Vice- Governor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor.- (a) If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the govemor or mayor , the vice-govemor or vice-mayor concerned shall become the govemor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs n the offices of the governor, vice-govemor, mayor, or vice-mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking

sanggunian member, shall become the governor, vice-govemor, mayor or vice- mayor, as the case may be. Subsequent vacancies in the said offce shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined herein. (b) If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office of the punong barangay, the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the punong barangay. (c) A tie between or among the highest ranking sanggunian members shall be resolved by the drawing of lots. (d) The successors as defined herein shall served only the unexpired tens of their predecessors. For purposes of this Chapter, a permanent vacmcy arises when an elective local oficials fills a higher vacant ofice, refuses to assume office, fails to qualify, dies, is removed from ofice, voluntarily resigns, or is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functions of his office. It may be observed that the last paragraph of the aforequoted provision enumerated tie specific causes of permanent vacancies. Such enumeration was followed by a general statement, to wit: "xxx is otherwise permanently incapacitated to discharge the functjms of his office." This general statement may refer to pemanent vacances brought about by of laws, such as civil interdiction or disqualification to hold office as an accessory penalty to criminal conviction. It may also refer to severe illness by the incumbent, such as the case of Sangguniang Barangay Member Escano, mich could effectively affect the performance of his duties and functions. With respect to severe illness of the incumbent, the normal course of things would be for him to either resign or file a leave of absence, whichever he opts to do so, in which case, the rule of succession may now be properly applied, whether referring to permanent or temporary vacancy. The problem, however, would anse if the ill incumbent will not resign or will not file a leave of absence but on the contrary, will insist to continue to hold Office when in the meantime his physical or mental sickness will not allow him to do so anymore. Parenthetically, there being no permanent or temporary vacancy to speak of, the rule on permanent vacancy under Section 44 of the Code or the rule on temporary vacancy under Section 46 of the same Code cannot yet be applied, It bears to stress that in situations like this, the Local Govemment Code did not empower any agency or oficial of the govemment to declare pemanent or temporary vacancy due to the illness of the incumbent. At this point, it bears to stress that due to lack of provision in the Local Govemment Code, the determination as to whether or not there is pemanent or temporary vacancy due to illness of the incumbent would necessarily become an adjudicatory matter, meaning, such declaration should be obtained from our courts of justice in order for the said court to adjudicate and apply the law involved It is in this regard, that we strongly suggest that in order for this hiatus not to be left without remedy as it would undoubtedly affect the operations of your barangay, you may invoke the aid of the Regional Trial Court, a court of general jurisdiction, seeking a declaration Wrsuant to the Rules of Court, as to whether or not your incumbent Sangguniang Barangay Member is still physically and mentally fit to discharge the functions of his office. It is only the court which can judicially declare a væancy in the ofice of the Sangguniang Barangay, whether permanent or temporary.

Should the court decides that there exists a permanent vacancy in your Sangunian, may we invite your attenbon to Sectjon 45 (a) (3) of the Local Governrnent Code of 1991 which provides for the proper procedure in filling up of permanent vacancies in the sanggunian. It states that: Sec. 45. Permanent Vacancies in the Sanggunian.- (a) Permanent vacancies in the sanggunian where automabc successions provided above (Section 44) do not apply shall be filed by appointment in the following manner: (3) The city or municipal mayor in the case of Sangguniang Barangay, upon recommendabon of the Sangguniang Barangay concerned. " In view of the foregoing, it is clear that in cases wherein automatic succession does not apply, a permanent væancy in the Sangguniang Barangay is to be filled by appointrnent by the Mayor, upon recommendation of the Sangguniang Barangay concemed. It must be however, that the required prior recommendabon is a collective act of the Sanggunian. Hope we have enlightened you accordingly. Manuel V. Biason Regional Director, San Fernando City La Union Legal:20/corz Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary: A JESUS QU V Director II
